key_insight: This review argues that medical AI should move beyond static prediction toward world models that simulate patient-state changes over time and under different interventions.
clinical_relevance: By modeling disease evolution and treatment-conditioned futures, these systems could help clinicians anticipate deterioration and compare care options for individual patients.
method: Frames medical world models around three linked parts: patient-state construction, clinical dynamics modeling, and intervention decision support.
Synthesizes work across foundation models, longitudinal modeling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins.
Maps how partial components can be combined into more complete perception–dynamics–planning systems.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a roadmap review that compares representative systems across related literature rather than reporting a single new clinical dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: A key challenge is ensuring that simulated rollouts are plausible and actually clinically useful, not just technically impressive.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
